defects.scenario: User removes a row in the Connected view while it is mounted. `remove()` (line 685-690) calls `this.retry(groupId)` — a single-group reload — and synchronously emits `contentChanged`. The hub's `onContentChanged()` (marketplace-hub.component.ts:168-171) responds by bumping `MarketplaceStateService.refreshTrigger`, which the surface's own `refreshEffect` (connected-surface.component.ts:406-410) picks up and triggers a SECOND full four-group `loadAll()`. None of `loadApps`/`loadPlugins`/`loadCommunity`/`loadMarketplaces` (lines 444-578) guards against out-of-order completion the way `decorateAppStatuses` does (line 629, `if (this.appGroups() !== groups) return;`), so two overlapping loads of the same group can resolve in either order with no sequencing. In the common case both RPCs return the same post-removal state so no wrong data is shown, but every removal issues roughly double the RPC traffic the plan's own budget allows ('at most 4 + 1 + n(oauth) reads per load', implementation-plan.md:577), and the race window is real and untested (connected-surface.component.spec.ts's refreshTrigger case at line 553 only exercises the reload path in isolation, not the retry+refresh interaction).
defects.fix: Either drop the direct `this.retry(groupId)` call in `remove()` and rely solely on the `refreshTrigger` fan-out already wired for every other surface, or give each `load*` method a request-epoch token and ignore a response whose token is stale, mirroring the guard `decorateAppStatuses` already uses.
